Differential topology provides shorter physical interconnection from its transistors’ source terminals to ground compared to a single-ended topology, and is also insensitive to the modeling inaccuracy of decoupling capacitors at 210GHz. In addition, the CGD-neutralization capacitor is realized by the CGD of a similar MOSFET to mitigate the mismatch between the neutralization capacitor and the main transistor’s CGD. Considering that the loss of the matching network makes the amplifier more stable, the PA’s main transistors are intentionally pushed to the edge of the stability region, resulting in higher gain. This has been achieved by properly sizing of the neutralization MOSFET. At frequencies close to fmax (i.e., at least one-third), the maximum Psat does not always increase as transistor size is increased, because it also highly depends on the device parasitics, as discussed in [5]. At 210GHz, the transistor size of the power stage is chosen to be 19.2μm with finger width of 0.64μm to maximize Psat. Considering that the quarter-wavelength is only around 180μm at 210GHz, a ground-shielded CPW line is utilized for the impedance matching network. All PA stages are interstage-matched to 50Ω to make the design more robust to uncertainties of passive components at this frequency as well as the length of interconnects; which, in turn, leads to more flexibility in layout. references.sentence: The TRX architecture is shown in Fig. 8.1.1.

To distribute a modulated differential signal from the PA driver to the 2×2 array, while maintaining differential signal integrity and avoiding EM-coupling due to cross-overs in layout, two Wilkinson power splitters followed by four Marchand baluns are employed (Fig. 8.1.1).
The non-coherent RX consists of an on-chip antenna, an LNA with a measured gain of 18dB, and a power detector (Fig. 8.1.1).
Shown in Fig. 8.1.2 are the fundamental double-stacked cross-coupled VCO and the OOK modulator.
The 30pH inductor LS in Fig. 8.1.2 mitigates the detrimental effect of parasitic capacitance of the bottom cross-coupled pair M1-M2.
The standalone VCO exhibits measured –13.5dBm output power, 8GHz tuning range (204.7 to 212.7GHz), and –80.9dBc/Hz phase noise at 1MHz offset at 209.2GHz (Fig. 8.1.2).
The three-stage differential PA with CGD-neutralization capacitance is shown in Fig. 8.1.3.

Occupying only 150×400μm2 (excluding pads), the PA circuit exhibits a measured peak gain of 15dB, a 3dB bandwidth of more than 14GHz, OP1dB of 2.7dBm, Psat of 4.6dBm, and a peak PAE of 6%, as shown in Fig. 8.1.3.
Figure 8.1.4 shows the schematic of the 7-stage differential CGD-neutralized LNA.
A continuous-wave (CW) wireless test between the TX and RX chips was performed over 3.5cm distance, and the measured SNR for different CW frequencies is shown in Fig. 8.1.5.
The complete measured performance of the TRX is summarized in Fig. 8.1.6.
The die micrographs of the TX and RX occupying areas of 1.4×2.5mm2 and 0.8×1.4mm2, respectively (including pads) are shown in Fig. 8.1.7.
